summary: Frontend-only final verification of the receipt PDF->JPEG change on the preview app (admin 9999999999/Admin@123, existing collection LFC-2608-1A2D1, read-only). Verified: (1) on-screen receipt amount renders as plain '500' / '13' with no rupee symbol, 'Rs' or 'INR' anywhere in .receipt-print-content across 5 receipts; (2) Download emits a real JPEG - suggested_filename 'Co-Daily-Collection-LFC-2608-1A2D1.jpg', magic ff d8 ff e0 (JFIF), EOI ff d9, 108,390 bytes, PIL reports JPEG 1044x1410 RGB; (3) captured image content matches the popup only - width 1044 = 348 CSS px * scale 3 (.receipt-print-content box 350x472), image contains company name, RECEIPT NO. + number, plain amount, VENDOR/PAYMENT MODE/RECEIVED AT/COLLECTED BY/REMARKS, dashed rule and thank-you line, and NO dashboard background, backdrop, close button or action buttons (visually inspected rasterised crop); (4) Share: with navigator.share/canShare stubbed, the app calls navigator.share with title 'Co. Daily Collection receipt' and files[0] = {name: Co-Daily-Collection-LFC-2608-1A2D1.jpg, type: image/jpeg, size: 108,919} - with navigator.share deleted it falls back to an identical .jpg download; (5) Print: window.open stubbed - called with target '_blank', document.write injects , the blob fetches back as type image/jpeg, 107,228 bytes, magic ff d8 ff e0, and both focus() and print() are invoked; with window.open forced to null the fallback downloads the same .jpg; (6) no jspdf/jsPDF/'.pdf' references remain in /app/frontend/src or package.json and jspdf is absent from node_modules - only html2canvas ^1.4.1 is used; (7) desktop 1920 and mobile 390x844 layouts render all three action buttons + close inside the viewport, buttons clickable, close works, disabled 'Preparing image...' state shown while capturing, 0 error elements and no page/console errors other than two pre-existing 401s from the pre-login /api/auth/me probe. ONE real defect found: the exported JPEG has no bottom/side padding, so the last line 'Thank you for your payment.' is clipped mid-glyph at the very bottom edge (last dark pixel row = 1409 of 1410) and all labels/values sit flush against x=0.

ui_bugs.issue: The exported image is clipped at the bottom: the thank-you line's descenders and trailing period are cut off (canvas height 1410px vs element 472 CSS px * 3 = 1416px; last dark pixel row is 1409/1410). Also .receipt-print-content has zero padding (padding lives on .receipt-dialog, which is excluded from the capture), so 'VENDOR', 'TEST_auth_identity' etc. touch the left edge at x=0 and the brand/amount have no top/bottom breathing room. Fix: add padding (e.g. 22-26px) to .receipt-print-content (or a dedicated export wrapper), and/or pass an explicit height/windowHeight of Math.ceil(scrollHeight)+pad to html2canvas so the final text line is never truncated.

integration_issues.issue: No defect. All three paths produce JPEG blobs of the same receipt-only content (download 108,390 B 1044x1410; share fallback 108,934 B 1044x1407; print fallback 106,950 B 1044x1407; mobile 103,664 B 879x1410 - sizes differ only by JPEG re-encode/subpixel rounding). Share passes a File of type image/jpeg; print's blob URL resolves to image/jpeg and print() is called; both fall back to the identical .jpg download.

issues: No blocking issue: dialog centred, opaque white, all 5 detail rows visible, buttons full-width and clickable, close button reachable, layout fits within the mobile viewport (dialog 354x692 in 844px height).
Exported JPEG has no padding and clips the last text line (see ui_bugs).

design_issues.screen: Dashboard 'Collections trend' chart (pre-existing, out of scope)
issues: Y-axis tick labels are inconsistent: some render as "'0.004k" (stray apostrophe instead of the rupee glyph) while others render '₹0.001k'.

action_items: Add padding to the captured .receipt-print-content (and/or an explicit padded height for html2canvas) so 'Thank you for your payment.' is not clipped and text is not flush to the image edges.
Optional: pre-existing chart y-axis label shows "'0.004k" instead of the rupee glyph on some ticks.
critical_code_review_comments: createReceiptImage relies on the element's own box; since .receipt-print-content has no padding, html2canvas' rounded height truncates the final line. Prefer a wrapper with padding or pass width/height explicitly (Math.ceil(el.scrollHeight)+pad).
runImageAction swallows the underlying error (only a generic message is shown) - consider console.error(error) to keep diagnosability while keeping the friendly UI message.

printReceipt writes the image with document.write and relies on printWindow.onload; assigning onload after document.close() can miss the event for a same-document blob img in some browsers - a fallback setTimeout print (as the previous PDF version had) would be safer on slow mobile.
No jspdf import or dependency remains; html2canvas is the only export dependency - clean.

success_rate.frontend: 6/7 verification items fully pass; 1 MEDIUM visual defect (exported JPEG clipped/unpadded)

seed_data_creation: None. Read-only: admin login, opened existing receipts. Artifacts written to /tmp only (receipt_download.jpg, receipt_share_fallback.jpg, receipt_print_fallback.jpg, receipt_mobile.jpg).
context_for_next_testing_agent: JPEG regression recipe: Playwright -> login admin -> click first [data-testid^=view-receipt-] -> assert [data-testid=receipt-amount] has no ₹/Rs -> page.expect_download on [data-testid=receipt-download-button] and save to /tmp, then verify magic bytes ff d8 ff e0 + PIL size. For Share, stub navigator.share/canShare in page.evaluate and read window.__shared for files[0].type. For Print, stub window.open to return a fake window recording html/focus/print, then fetch the blob: URL out of the injected to assert type image/jpeg. Known open defect: exported JPEG clips the thank-you line (no padding on .receipt-print-content).
rca_of_the_issue: Clipping RCA: html2canvas captures only .receipt-print-content, whose box ends exactly at the thank-you line's line-box bottom (thanks.bottom - content.bottom = 0 px, because the paragraph's margin-bottom:18px collapses out of the unpadded parent). The produced canvas is 1410px = floor of 472 CSS px * 3 minus rounding, i.e. ~2 CSS px shorter than the element, so the final line's descenders/period fall outside the raster. Adding padding to the captured node (or an explicit padded height) removes both the clipping and the flush-to-edge look.
